prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideology-neutral, no names)

Europe and international
- Hold a referendum on the final EU deal, with an option to remain.
- Seek close EU ties: single market/customs union access, rights for EU/UK citizens, Erasmus+, security cooperation (Europol/EAW), research funding.
- Maintain high environmental, social and consumer standards post‑Brexit.
- Spend 0.7% of GNI on aid; tighten arms export controls; support multilateral institutions.
- Defence: spend 2% of GDP; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced posture; boost cyber capability; enhance European defence cooperation.

Health and social care
- Add 1p to Income Tax (and dividends) ringfenced for NHS and social care; develop a dedicated health and care tax.
- Create an independent health and care budget watchdog; cross‑party convention; integrate NHS and social care budgets by 2020.
- End public sector pay cap; restore nurse bursaries; workforce strategy.
- Mental health parity: national waiting time standards, crisis care, perinatal support, end out‑of‑area placements.
- Prevention: obesity strategy, sugar reduction targets, tobacco levy, minimum alcohol pricing (subject to outcome), PrEP on NHS, antimicrobial resistance plan.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding in real terms; increase Pupil Premium; fair national formula.
- Triple Early Years Pupil Premium; raise early years quality standards.
- No new selective schools; restore local place planning powers; allow Ofsted to inspect academy chains.
- End teachers’ pay cap; require/expand QTS and high‑quality CPD.
- Core curriculum including PSHE, financial literacy, first aid, mental health, and inclusive SRE; protect arts; strengthen vocational routes and careers advice.
- Reinstate maintenance grants; review higher education finance; widen participation; protect research links.
- Expand apprenticeships; lifelong learning accounts; meet basic skills needs by 2030.

Economy, tax, business and work
- Eliminate day‑to‑day deficit by 2020; borrow to invest £100bn in housing, hyperfast fibre (FTTP), schools, hospitals, and transport (HS2, Crossrail 2, rail electrification).
- Expand a Housing & Infrastructure Development Bank.
- Reverse selected tax cuts; strengthen anti‑avoidance; review business rates; consider land value taxation.
- Expand British Business Bank; start‑up allowance; reduce regulatory uncertainty.
- Modernise employment rights for gig economy; curb zero‑hours abuses; scrap tribunal fees; promote living wage and pay transparency; enhance worker participation and employee ownership.

Housing, communities and welfare
- Build 300,000 homes/year by 2022; at least 10 new garden cities; lift council/Housing Association borrowing caps; strengthen affordable housing obligations; deter land‑banking; allow higher council tax on second homes.
- Renting: ban letting fees; cap deposits; longer tenancies; Help to Rent loans; Rent to Own; tenant first refusal; stronger rogue landlord licensing.
- Childcare: extend free hours (including for 2‑year‑olds); expand Shared Parental Leave; flexible work as a day‑one right.
- Welfare: uprate working‑age benefits with inflation; scrap two‑child limit and bedroom tax; improve LHA; reform disability assessments; limit Winter Fuel Payment to non‑higher‑rate taxpayers.

Transport
- Rail franchise reform with passenger focus; allow public/mutual bids; electrification; HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2; East West Rail; shift freight to rail.
- Young Person’s Bus Discount Card (16–21); devolve bus powers; smart ticketing; improve cycling/walking.
- Strategic airports policy with no net increase in UK runways; focus on regional capacity.

Environment, energy, farming and waste
- Five green laws framework; insulate 4m homes by 2022; restore zero‑carbon homes standard; expand community energy; 60% electricity from renewables by 2030; oppose fracking; maintain Euratom; support CCS.
- Air quality plan: diesel scrappage; ban new diesel car/small van sales by 2025; expand low‑emission zones; build EV infrastructure.
- Nature and farming: flood‑prevention fund; Nature Act with binding targets; tree planting; stronger animal welfare; reform farm support toward public goods; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; national plan for sustainable fisheries.
- Zero‑Waste Act: resource‑efficiency targets; 70% recycling by 2022; coffee cup charge; reform landfill/incineration taxes.

Rights, justice, immigration and asylum
- Retain Human Rights Act and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; media plurality/FOI reforms.
- Policing: +£300m/year; end pay cap; body cameras; replace PCCs with boards.
- Justice: Victims’ Bill; presumption against short sentences; expand restorative justice; improve legal aid; protect judicial review.
- Terrorism: targeted, overseen surveillance; replace Prevent; roll back bulk powers; protect encryption.
- Drugs: end imprisonment for possession; regulate cannabis for adults; focus on traffickers.
- Immigration: efficient system with skills focus; remove students from net migration stats; STEM post‑study visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL funding.
- Asylum: expand safe routes; 50,000 resettlement places; 3,000 unaccompanied children; 28‑day detention limit; faster decisions; work after 6 months; protect those at risk due to sexual orientation or gender identity.

Constitution and devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections; reform Lords; cap donations; strengthen lobbying rules; leaders’ debates; improve expense rules.
- Constitutional convention for a federal UK; devolve repatriated powers; further powers for Wales; support NI settlement and arrangements; English‑only legislative stage on proportional basis; devolution on demand; retain Barnett with fair floor for Wales.
